CONDITIONAL: CONDITIONAL. Sprint 24's own diff (9d5af65) meets every requirement R1-R9 and
is the cleanest work I've audited on this project. It is blocked by a broken
repo state it did not create.

BLOCKING CONDITION (not sprint 24's code):
`npm run lint` fails with 25 errors, all @typescript-eslint/no-require-imports,
all in scripts/install.js and scripts/launcher/*.js. Those files are new in the
PRECEDING commit e14d633 ("Tooling housekeeping"), not in 9d5af65. Verified:
`npx eslint app lib` is completely clean, and none of those paths existed at
db915b8. .github/workflows/ci.yml line 22 runs `npm run lint` as its FIRST step,
so pushing this sprint puts CI red on the very first job and LiveQA gets
nothing deployable to test. The sprint's own acceptance criteria require lint
clean; it is not clean, so I cannot record a PASS.
Fix belongs to tooling, not to this sprint: add "scripts/**" to globalIgnores in
eslint.config.mjs (same rationale as the existing "docs/design/**" ignore -- Node
CJS launcher scripts are not app source), or convert the launchers to ESM. Per
CLAUDE.md's "Changes to this repo's own tooling" that is not sprint work, but it
must land and be committed before sprint 24 ships. Re-run /sprint-qa1 24 once
lint is green; I will re-audit against the new HEAD.

REQUIREMENTS COVERAGE -- all met:
R1 met. "Cast"->"Cast the chart", "Save this reading"->"See the full reading",
"Read the chart"->"Write the horoscope". Greps for the old labels return only
explanatory comments, nothing user-facing. No digits in any of the three labels.
R2 met. Four states reachable, driven by one `completedSteps` 0-3 number.
/chart uses `positions ? 1 : 0`, /reading uses `horoscope ? 3 : 2`. Not
hardcoded per route -- this was the sprint's headline risk and it was handled
correctly.
R3 met, and this is the one I checked hardest. No "use client" added or removed
anywhere in the diff. No useState/useEffect/useRef introduced (the only grep
hits are the word "useState" inside a doc comment). app/chart/page.tsx still
opens with `import`, still a server component. FlowIndicator is a pure function
of its single prop.
R4 met. One module, app/components/FlowIndicator.tsx, imported by both routes.
No duplication.
R5 met. app/layout.tsx untouched by the commit.
R6 met. "not read yet" gone from both sites (ReadingPanel.tsx:70 and
page.tsx:392). IdleBlock accent now reads "write the horoscope", matching the
button. "Cast a new reading" -> "Cast a new chart" with the reasoning written
into the comment at ReadingPanel.tsx:128 -- the deliberate decision R6 asked to
see, not left ambiguous.
R7 met. Commit touches no file under lib/llm/ and not app/chart/actions.ts.
"Try again", "Copy link"/"Copied" intact.
R8 met. package.json untouched, globals.css untouched (still 20 --om- tokens).
flow-indicator.module.css defines zero new custom properties and consumes only
--om-bone, --om-bone-dim, --om-grey-dim, --om-ink, --om-rule-strong,
--om-verdigris, --font-mono -- every one verified to already exist
(--font-mono via next/font in layout.tsx:20).
R9 plausible statically. flex-wrap + flexible connector (flex 1 1 20px,
min 12px, max 44px) instead of a fixed layout, and the mobile block correctly
adds flex-shrink: 0 to .flowSlot, matching what Sprint 20 needed for .dateBand
in the same fixed-height flex column. Real proof is LiveQA's.

CODE QUALITY:
Tests: adequate and honestly scoped. stepState() extracted as a pure function
and unit tested across all four states, with the reasoning for testing it
directly (no React rendering setup in this project) written down rather than
silently skipped. 188/188 pass. I'd rather see this than a fake render test.
Error handling: nothing new introduced, nothing swallowed. Correct for a diff
that is presentational by design.
Standards: comments explain WHY and cite requirement numbers. The chart.module.css
comment referring to the old labels was updated rather than left to rot -- that
is the kind of thing that usually gets missed.
Security: no new user input, no new interpolation, no dangerouslySetInnerHTML.
Sprint 18/19 guarantees intact -- escaped horoscope rendering, no markdown
library, isSafeExternalUrl still on event URLs, fonts still via next/font.
Build clean.

NON-BLOCKING ISSUE (fix it while you're in there, don't make a sprint of it):
[low] app/components/FlowIndicator.tsx:60,64 -- `styles[state]` renders the
literal string "undefined" as a class name when state === "ahead". The CSS
module defines .marker.done/.current and .label.done/.current but no .ahead, so
styles.ahead is undefined and the DOM gets class="..._marker__hash undefined" on
every ahead step -- which is both steps on a cold /chart. Visually correct,
because the base .marker/.label already carry the ahead appearance, so nothing
looks wrong. It is still shipping garbage into the markup. Either define an
empty .ahead in the module or fall back with `styles[state] ?? ""`.

Scope discipline: the sprint declared .claude/, scripts/, and CLAUDE.md out of
scope and 9d5af65 touches none of them. Correct. The lint breakage arrived on
the adjacent housekeeping commit, which is exactly the risk this sprint's own
Dependencies section flagged -- settle the tooling tree before building app code
on it. It got committed, but committed red is not settled.

PASS: PASS (round 2). Audited at HEAD a783d6a, working tree clean, everything
committed. Both round-1 conditions cleared, and cleared in the right places.

SPRINT FILE: re-read fresh before this verdict. `git diff 9d5af65..HEAD` on
docs/sprints/2-in-progress/sprint-24_step-labels-and-flow-indicator.md is empty
and the tree is clean, so the file is byte-identical to what I audited in round
1. No mid-build amendment. Requirements audited are the current ones.

BLOCKING CONDITION FROM ROUND 1 -- CLEARED (7a1413a):
eslint.config.mjs adds "scripts/**" to globalIgnores with the reasoning written
in: standalone Node CJS tooling, not Next.js app source, same rationale as the
existing docs/design/** entry. Correct fix and correctly scoped -- I checked the
whole directory and scripts/ holds only .sh, .py and standalone .js launcher
files, nothing that should ever have been linted as app source, so the ignore
gives up no real coverage. It also loses nothing that previously passed: before
e14d633 that directory was .py and .sh only, which eslint never touched.
Landed as its own tooling commit, separate from the app commit, per CLAUDE.md's
"Changes to this repo's own tooling". That separation is right and I want it
noted -- the app diff stays a clean app diff.

All four CI steps (.github/workflows/ci.yml) now verified green locally, in CI's
own order:
  npm run lint       clean, zero errors (was 25)
  npm run typecheck  clean
  npm run test       188/188 across 19 files
  npm run build      compiled, 4 routes generated

NON-BLOCKING ISSUE FROM ROUND 1 -- FIXED (a783d6a):
.marker.ahead / .label.ahead now defined in flow-indicator.module.css, so
styles["ahead"] resolves to a real class and the literal string "undefined"
no longer reaches the DOM. Verified mechanically: every value stepState() can
return -- done, current, ahead -- now has both a .marker.* and a .label.* rule.
The declarations restate .marker/.label's own base colors, so zero visual
change, which is the correct fix: the state is now explicit rather than
implicit-by-omission, and the comment says exactly that. Good fix.

REQUIREMENTS -- all met, re-verified at HEAD across the cumulative app diff
(db915b8..HEAD touches exactly 8 files, all under app/):
R1 met. Three labels renamed; no old label survives outside explanatory
comments; no digits in any button label.
R2 met. Four states, one completedSteps 0-3 number, /chart `positions ? 1 : 0`
and /reading `horoscope ? 3 : 2`. Not hardcoded per route.
R3 met. No "use client" anywhere in app/components/ or app/chart/page.tsx. No
hooks introduced. Indicator is a pure function of one prop.
R4 met. One module imported by both routes.
R5 met. app/layout.tsx absent from the cumulative diff entirely.
R6 met. Both "not read yet" sites fixed, IdleBlock accent matches the button,
"Cast a new chart" decision documented in the diff.
R7 met. No lib/llm/ file and no actions.ts in the diff. "Try again",
"Copy link"/"Copied" intact.
R8 met. package.json and app/globals.css both absent from the cumulative diff.
No new custom property, no new dependency.
R9 statically plausible -- flex-wrap, flexible connector, flex-shrink: 0 in the
mobile block. Real proof is LiveQA's at width <900px.
Sprint 18/19 guarantees intact.

CODE QUALITY: unchanged from round 1 and still the assessment I gave then --
stepState() extracted and honestly unit tested across all four states rather
than faked through a rendering setup this project doesn't have; comments explain
why and cite requirement numbers; stale comments updated rather than left to
rot. Nothing swallowed, no new input surface, no new interpolation.

Bookkeeping note, not a defect: a783d6a also carries docs/sprints/state/
sprint-24.json. That is my own round-1 verdict as the lifecycle script wrote it,
committed rather than hand-edited. Correct -- sprint state is tracked data and
belongs in git.

CLEARED TO SHIP. Dev Team runs /sprint-dev-done 24, then Pipeman ships
a783d6a. LiveQA still owns the four things a static read cannot settle: that
casting a date advances the indicator to step 2 on the same page, that
"Write the horoscope" still generates and persists end to end, that a written
reading reads "written", and that the indicator does not overflow below 900px.

PASS: PASS. Live browser test (headless Chromium via Playwright), production
https://my-little-racoon.vercel.app, 2026-08-28.

DEPLOYMENT NOTE, checked before testing: /api/health/db reports the live commit as
8fe82171506d5187e51be0af40b0b4be2cf51177 (8fe8217), NOT a783d6a. 8fe8217 is the
bookkeeping commit "Sprint 24: record ship (commit a783d6a)" sitting one above the
shipped commit. `git diff --stat a783d6a 8fe8217` = docs/sprints/state/sprint-24.json
only, and the app/ and lib/ tree hashes are byte-identical across the two
(app e5692dfef63140a6ad48693a26d05c4d16da92f6, lib 23ecdeaadd17586b4d474884c92a9bee2417787e).
Production is therefore serving a783d6a's application code and this test is valid for it.

EVERY LIVEQA CRITERION FROM THE SPRINT FILE -- ALL PASS:

1. /chart cold. PASS. Indicator: step 1 marker+label class "current", aria-current="step";
steps 2 and 3 class "ahead". Container aria-label verbatim: "Progress through chart,
reading, and horoscope". Button verbatim: "CAST THE CHART". No digit in the label.

2. Submit a date -- the sprint's headline risk. PASS. Filled 1969-07-20, clicked
"Cast the chart", landed on /chart?date=1969-07-20 with positions rendered and the
indicator advanced ON THE SAME PAGE: "checkmark CHART = DONE | 2 READING = CURRENT |
3 HOROSCOPE = AHEAD". Second button verbatim: "SEE THE FULL READING". Page states the
instant verbatim: "Positions calculated for 1969-07-20T12:00:00.000Z - every date is
evaluated at 12:00 UTC, not a specific hour you provide."

3. Press "See the full reading". PASS. Reached
/reading/c512f1ab-f8ba-4b65-b280-c500faed4bba. Indicator: CHART DONE, READING DONE,
HOROSCOPE CURRENT. Status label reads verbatim "NOT WRITTEN YET" (uppercase by CSS).
"not read yet" absent from all three routes.

4. Press "Write the horoscope" -- the regression proof. PASS. Generation ran end to end,
2.8s, three-to-four paragraphs, status flipped to "WRITTEN", indicator went
DONE/DONE/DONE. In-flight state observed 400ms after click: button disabled=true,
panel reads "WRITING / The reading is being written. / gpt-4o-mini - temperature 0.9".

5. Reload the written reading. PASS. Text byte-identical to pre-reload, indicator
DONE/DONE/DONE, "NOT WRITTEN YET" absent, status reads "WRITTEN". Persisted.

6. Mobile below 900px, both routes. PASS. Tested 899/700/500/390/360/320px. The
indicator never overflows its viewport at any width (measured right edge vs clientWidth)
and wraps legibly -- two lines at 390px, a centered vertical stack at 320-360px cold.
See the pre-existing finding below re: a horizontal scrollbar on /chart?date= that the
indicator does NOT cause.

7. Force a generation failure. NOT VERIFIED -- not reachable, and the criterion is
written "if reachable". Generation is a server-side call; I cannot induce an LLM failure
from the client. Aborting the server-action POST at the network layer replaced the
document with Chrome's own network-error page ("Reload"/"Back"), which exercises the
browser, not the app's error state. I am recording this as untested rather than passed.

ADDITIONAL LIVE CONFIRMATIONS:

R5 confirmed live: /reading/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000 returns HTTP 404 with
body "404 / This page could not be found." and NO flow indicator -- the indicator is not
in the root layout.

R6 confirmed live: "Cast a new chart" navigates to /chart and the indicator resets to
CURRENT/AHEAD/AHEAD at both 1280px and 390px. Old vocabulary swept: "Save this reading",
"Read the chart", "not read yet", "Cast a new reading" -- zero hits in rendered text or
HTML on /chart cold, /chart?date=, and a written reading.

R7 confirmed live: "COPY LINK" present on the reading page at desktop and mobile.

R2 derivation confirmed negatively: with date=1699-12-31, 2101-01-01, not-a-date, and
1969-13-45, positions do not render and the indicator correctly stays at step 1 current
(CURRENT/AHEAD/AHEAD). The state follows the data, it is not hardcoded per route.

BREAK ATTEMPTS -- nothing broke:
Blank-date submit: stays on /chart, no crash, indicator unchanged. Double-click "Cast the
chart": single navigation, positions render once. Rapid repeat clicks on "Write the
horoscope" as a real user: button is genuinely disabled=true from 150ms onward, all three
follow-up clicks REJECTED as not clickable -- no double-generation race. Forcing five
clicks through with Playwright's force flag (bypasses the disabled check, which a real
user cannot do) still produced clean non-duplicated output that survived reload. Zero
console errors, zero page errors, zero failed requests across every run.

AI OUTPUT -- 3 consistency runs, same date, fresh readings:
Run 1 (3.2s, 4 paragraphs) / Run 2 (1.9s, 3 paragraphs) / Run 3 (4.1s, 4 paragraphs).
STABLE in substance -- all three name the same three aspects in the same order (Jupiter
conjunct Uranus, Moon sextile Mars, Mercury trine Neptune); paragraph count varies 3-4.
No garbling, no interleaving, no duplicated or truncated text. Every aspect claim checks
out against the page's OWN position table: Jupiter 00 deg 41' Libra and Uranus 00 deg 40'
Libra = conjunction (run 3 even says "in Libra", correct); Moon 03 deg 29' Libra to Mars
02 deg 43' Sagittarius = 60 deg sextile; Mercury 25 deg 06' Cancer to Neptune 26 deg 01'
Scorpio = 120 deg trine; Sun 27 deg 34' Cancer to Neptune = trine. No fabricated aspects.
The historical claim matches the page's own Wikipedia block and the "(source)" link
resolves HTTP 200 to en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11. Not a dead link.

TWO PRE-EXISTING DEFECTS FOUND -- NOT introduced by sprint 24, NOT blocking it. Logging
them so they are not lost; they deserve their own sprint:

(a) MEDIUM. Horizontal scrollbar on /chart?date=... below roughly 362px viewport.
At 360px documentElement scrollWidth=361 vs clientWidth=360; at 320px scrollWidth=341 vs
clientWidth=320, and the card is clipped 21px off the left edge. The single overflowing
element is <main class="chart-module__card">, pinned at 361.9px. NOT the indicator: the
cold /chart card, which carries the same indicator, shrinks to 231px with no scrollbar at
any width. The floor is the positions <table> min-content width of 271.9px plus 44px
padding each side. Unaffected at 390px and above.

(b) MEDIUM. Two "Cast a new chart" controls render simultaneously on a written reading
below 900px. Measured: 1280px and 1000px render exactly one (the mobileWrittenFooter is
display:none); at 899, 700, 500, 390 and 360px BOTH render -- the sticky readingFooter
one at x=32 and the mobileWrittenFooter one at x=117, side by side in the footer.
Attribution checked: sprint 24's diff (db915b8..a783d6a) contains no added or removed CSS
line touching .readingFooter or .mobileWrittenFooter, and both elements already existed
at db915b8. Sprint 24 only renamed the text inside them, so this predates it and the two
duplicates previously read identically as "Cast a new reading".

(c) LOW, cosmetic. At 390px on /chart?date=, the indicator wraps after "2 READING" and
leaves a dangling connector dash at the end of the first line with nothing after it.

ONE THING I CHECKED AND CLEARED rather than reporting: at 390px a full-page screenshot
makes the horoscope look truncated behind the sticky footer. It is not. The text lives in
an internal scroll container (.rightColumn, scrollHeight 1143 vs clientHeight 381); I
scrolled it to the bottom and confirmed every paragraph is reachable and fully legible.
Sprint 19/20's fixed-height column design, working as intended.

RECOMMENDATION: sprint 24 ships. The four-state indicator, the three renames, the
vocabulary fix and horoscope generation all verified live. Findings (a) and (b) are real
and user-visible but predate this sprint and belong in a follow-up; criterion 7 is
recorded as untested, not passed.
